name: Gundestrup Cauldron

attributes.attribute: found in the Danish bog in 1891
dates to the 2nd or 1st century BC
a figure in the Celtic manner

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Gundestrup Cauldron is a great silver vessel of the old world. Workers found it in a peat bog in Denmark in 1891. Someone had put it there, perhaps as a gift to the gods or as a hiding from danger. Scholars date the bowl to the second or first century before the common era. Many call the vessel a Celtic work. Figures in relief show a goddess on a cart and a horned god. These images echo the ones the Celts knew in other lands.

okr.objective: Report the find and the carved figures of the cauldron.
